title: Scheme and morphism conventions
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. It is *proper* if it is separated, locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and universally closed, with separated and universally closed as in [def-weil-proper-morphism]; since a universally closed morphism is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-quasi-compact], this is the notion *proper* (separated, of finite type, universally closed) of [def-weil-proper-morphism]; *finite* if it is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a finite $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; an *immersion* if it factors as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]; *surjective* if surjective on underlying spaces [def-weil-surjective-morphism]; and *étale* [def-weil-etale-morphism] if locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. A scheme is *affine* [def-pc-scheme] if it is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$, with $\operatorname{Spec}$ as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum].
